title: Fix a FastAPI Dockerfile
problem: A colleague's Dockerfile for a FastAPI app builds, but it uses a floating base image, bakes an OAuth secret into the image, runs as root and starts uvicorn in shell form. Fix it so it follows the four rules from the lesson.
requirements: Base image: python with a pinned version tag that includes the Python version and the slim variant (not latest)
No ENV or ARG whose name looks like a secret (SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY)
The container runs as a non-root user: create it with useradd in a RUN, then switch with USER (a numeric UID also works)
CMD in exec form (a JSON array) running uvicorn app.main:app on host 0.0.0.0 and port 8000
contract: A file named Dockerfile in this folder. The app lives in app/main.py as `app = FastAPI()`, and requirements.txt sits next to the Dockerfile.
expectedBehavior: All four static checks in test_dockerfile.py pass. (With Docker, `docker build -t api .` then `docker run -p 8000:8000 -e OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=... api` would serve the app as a non-root user.)
edgeCases: A tag like 3.12-slim pins the minor version; 3.12.16-slim pins the patch too. latest or no tag fails
CMD with single quotes is not valid JSON, so Docker treats it as shell form
USER root or USER 0 is still root
USER with a name that was never created
hints: Conceptual: everything in a Dockerfile ends up in the image that anyone with pull access can inspect, and the final USER and CMD decide how the container's main process runs.
Specific: change four lines: the FROM tag, delete the ENV line, add a user and switch to it after pip install, and turn CMD into a JSON array of strings with double quotes.

Implementation: FROM python:<version>-slim with a version from Docker Hub; RUN groupadd -r NAME && useradd --no-log-init -r -g NAME NAME; USER NAME; CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", ...] with each argument as its own string.
evaluation: pip install still runs before USER (it writes to system site-packages)
The secret is not moved somewhere else in the file (e.g. into a RUN export)
